standard.title: Leadership and collaboration
standard.description: practise and apply leadership, collaboration and group decision-making processes when participating in a range of physical activities
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have participated positively in groups and teams by contributing to group activities, encouraging others and negotiating roles and responsibilities (Y5-6). They can participate constructively but have not yet been expected to undertake explicit leadership roles or apply group decision-making processes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students practise and apply leadership, collaboration and group decision-making processes when participating in a range of physical activities.

nodes.label: Understanding leadership and collaboration roles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify different leadership and collaboration roles, describe what each involves, and explain how the roles contribute to team and group outcomes.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two distinct roles (one leadership, one collaboration) and explain what each contributes to a team or group outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of leadership and collaboration roles across different physical activity contexts; explain how roles distribute responsibility and contribute to cohesion and success; distinguish between formal and informal leadership.
wider: Investigate how leadership styles differ across competitive team sport and cooperative outdoor activities, examining what makes each style effective in its context
Explore how cultural understandings of leadership and collective decision-making influence group dynamics in physical activity contexts from different communities

response_modes.reason: Encountering diverse role types prevents students from developing a single fixed model of leadership. Breadth here builds adaptability.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two roles in a team or group physical activity context (including one leadership role)
Explains what each role contributes to the team or group outcome

nodes.label: Reading group dynamics
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret verbal, physical and situational cues from others in a team or group and respond appropriately to support positive group functioning.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one verbal or non-verbal cue from a teammate or group member during a physical activity and describe an appropriate response.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret verbal, physical and situational cues across different group contexts; respond adaptively to the feelings and motives of others; recognise when group cohesion is being helped or hindered and adjust responses accordingly.
wider: Reflect on how verbal, physical and situational cues are interpreted differently in competitive vs cooperative physical activity contexts, and what this means for leadership and collaboration responses
Investigate how awareness of group dynamics in physical activity contexts connects to leadership and collaboration in other areas of school and community life
nodes.hinge_reason: Effective leadership and collaboration depend on situational awareness — students who cannot read group dynamics will apply generic responses that may undermine rather than support the group. Decision-making quality directly depends on cue interpretation.

response_modes.reason: Explicitly teach cue interpretation as a skill — what cues are available (verbal, physical, situational), what do they signal, and what response options are available? Use real physical activity scenarios as the teaching context.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one verbal or non-verbal cue from a team or group member
Describes an appropriate response to the cue that supports positive group functioning

nodes.label: Practising leadership and collaboration
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adopt varied leadership and collaboration roles across physical activities, contributing actively to group decision-making and reflecting on how their actions affected outcomes.
nodes.minimum_width: Adopt at least one leadership or collaboration role in a physical activity and describe one way your actions in that role contributed to the group or team outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Adopt varied roles (leader, collaborator, planner) across multiple physical activities; apply group decision-making processes; reflect on how specific actions initiated in each role led to outcomes; support peers in planning and executing physical activities.
wider: Plan and lead a physical activity for a peer group from design through to facilitation, evaluating the leadership decisions made at each stage
Undertake the role of activity planner for a team, developing a collaborative decision-making process and reflecting on how group input shaped the final plan

response_modes.reason: Leadership and collaboration are dispositional capabilities that develop through repetition across varied contexts — students need multiple role experiences, not a single leadership task.

Planning and leading physical activities integrates role awareness, cue-reading and decision-making into coordinated action. Structured reflection after each role experience is essential to consolidate the learning.

success_criteria: Adopts at least one leadership or collaboration role in a physical activity
Describes at least one specific action taken in that role
Reflects on how that action contributed to the team or group outcome
